action: Diagnose why a drawing cannot be placed through this harness, after four techniques across two sessions
response: ⭐ ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED THIS PASS: BrowserStack App Live translates a synthetic pointerdown/pointerup pair into a LONG PRESS on the device regardless of the dwell I specify. Proof: a 70ms synthetic 'tap' on the Safari dock icon opened iOS's app context menu (Remove App / Edit Home Screen / New Tab) rather than launching Safari. Mitigation found: a 15ms press plus a 2px move ('micro-tap') is interpreted as a real tap and made every DOM control work — Safari launch, address bar, login fields, Log In, the Tools sheet, Draw on chart, and arming the Horizontal tool all succeeded with it. ⛔ BUT the same micro-tap on the CHART CANVAS never places a drawing, and neither does a 12ms zero-movement tap. Chart long-press DOES work (it opens the price sheet reliably), so input reaches the canvas — placement specifically does not fire.
result: A CHARACTERISED HARNESS LIMIT, CAUSE NOT ISOLATED - synthetic taps reach every DOM control but not the drawing overlay's placement path
url: self-attempted 2026-09-08, techniques: 70ms tap, 25ms tap, 15ms micro-tap with 2px move, 12ms zero-move tap; two device sessions
notes: ⛔⛔ DO NOT RECORD 'tap does not place a drawing on iOS' AS A UCT FINDING - a real finger was never tested here; every tap in this session was synthesised by the automation harness. ⛔ REASONING CORRECTED 2026-09-08 AFTER INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEW. This note previously argued the cause was BrowserStack's synthesised touch 'lacking a genuine touch identifier, a pressure/radius value, or a touchstart/touchend pair'. SOURCE RULES THAT OUT: placement is a React onPointerDown on the overlay canvas (ChartDrawingOverlay.jsx:2628 -> :1994), on a canvas set pointerEvents:'auto' whenever a tool is armed (:2596), and it reads ONLY pointerType, pointerId, clientX/Y and button - no touch identifier, no pressure, no touchstart/touchend. ⛔ THE SUPPORTING SYMMETRY WAS ALSO WRONG: 'chart long-press works on the same canvas' is false - with no tool armed the overlay canvas is pointerEvents:'none' and a different element handles the press, so the two gestures never shared a target. ⭐ AN UNTESTED CANDIDATE CAUSE EXISTS AND IS BETTER THAN THE ONE I GUESSED: activePointersRef.current.add(e.pointerId) with an early return when size > 1 (:2000-2001), drained ONLY by a pointerup that reaches the canvas (:2278), combined with touchAction:'none' + setPointerCapture on a canvas that flips to pointerEvents:'none' the instant a placement completes. A harness that leaks a pointerId would wedge exactly this way. ✅ THE HONEST RECORD: synthetic taps delivered by the harness to a real iPhone did not place a drawing with a tool armed, and the cause was NOT isolated between harness synthesis and UCT's own pointer accounting. ⭐ THE ROUTE THAT WOULD CLOSE IT: BrowserStack App Automate / Appium against the same bs-local URL, where driver.tap injects a real OS-level touch. It needs the account access key in the environment, which I must not read or print. One tap places the drawing; after that all four checks are one screenshot each.
